newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh's Ershad, party rebels ponder next move.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh's Ershad, party rebels ponder next move.

text.p: Bangladesh's former president Hossain Mohammad Ershad, his political career in shambles over a love affair, might expel rebels from his Jatiya Party who are trying to strip him of its leadership, his associates said.
"Chairman Ershad is taking necessary steps, which might include the expulsion of party rebels," one of his associates told reporters on Saturday.
"Ershad is having discussions with loyalists (in the party) and charting his next moves. He is a fighter and won't give up easily," said the associate, who declined to be named.

Ershad's leadership came under threat after three top leaders of the Jatiya Party, the country's third-biggest political group, asked him to quit his post after he publicly confessed of an extramarital love affair.

The 68-year-old army lieutanant-general turned president, ousted in a popular uprising in 1990 and later jailed until this January, has since moved swiftly to defend his career by dropping Zinat Hossain, his lover for 14 years and a fellow Jatiya Party legislator, from the party's presidium.
"But it's too little, too late now," said leading Jatiya rebel Kazi Zafar Ahmed, a former prime minister.
"I don't see any reason for us to stop short of his resignation," Ahmed told Reuters on Saturday.
"We will discuss the latest situation at a meeting later on Saturday and decide on our next move. We have had enough of Ershad."
The rift in the Jatiya party surfaced in March when Ershad expelled Ahmed from the party after he had criticised the government's policies towards India. But Ahmed soon managed a comeback.
Ershad triggered a new controversy last week by telling a Dhaka newspaper that he had proposed to Zinat, wife of former industry seceretary Mosharraf Hossain.
A few weeks earlier, Ershad had stirred a family dispute by celebrating his birthday with Zinat, instead of his wife Begum Roushan.
The rebels, taking advantage of his personal problems, asked Ershad on Thursday night to transfer the party's leadership to them.
Ershad had "turned the party into his own property and indulged in activities that not only tarnished his personal image but disturbed the party's rank and file", they said in a statement.

Dhaka's daily Ajker Kagoj reported on Saturday that several radical Moslem groups have demanded that Ershad and Zinat should be punished for adultery according to Islamic law, suggesting they should be lashed in public.
